survivingClaim: Paper lane; nothing new about zeros of zeta. Of twelve catalogued literature inequalities that consume a Hecke eigen-relation or exact local factor, none has all hypotheses met by O1, O2 or O3 at a zero in the open strip. Lemma T (proved, confirmed): for a torus parameter every L(s,Pi,r x chi) is a product of shifted Dirichlet L-functions and the rightmost pole minus the rightmost local/gamma pole abscissa equals 1 for every parameter and r, so the pole-position hypothesis "rightmost pole on Re s=1" is equivalent to the exponent-0 conclusion (the simplicity part of POLE1 never holds for n>=2). Proposition E (classical argument, confirmed): the Eisenstein-series proof of zeta(1+it)!=0 is the one entry met in full with a zero-specific hypothesis, at Re rho=1; in the strip the missing hypothesis is xi(2-rho)=0, false by the Euler product. For O2 only E4 has its hypotheses met iff beta=1/2; the other entries also fail L2/CUSP at every beta; theta-orthogonality is a hypothesis of none of the twelve. For O3 the eigen-relation fails (relative to row G26). The isobaric (non-torus) case T4 is argued, not proved. Catalogue completeness and attributions are recalled, not source-checked.

lesson: A zero in the strip removes the constant-term coefficient whose argument is in the strip, never the one right of 1. The template "zero supplies cuspidality, a theorem contradicts it" is the classical proof on Re s = 1 and stops there. Inequalities that read an object through L(s,Pi,r x chi) cannot bound a torus parameter: pole and local pole move together for every r. Every catalogued bound below 1/2 needs L2, pole at 1, spectral membership or unitarity.
